settings.title: Settings
settings.placeholder: "{category}" settings are planned for a later phase

general.languageHint: English is the default. Changes apply immediately (no restart). Chinese, Spanish, French and German catalogs are community-maintained; a missing string falls back to English.

agent.providerHint: Uses your existing subscription sign-in. No API key is needed (authentication is delegated to the Claude Code CLI sign-in).
agent.cliMissingHint: Check that {command} works in a terminal, or set a path in "Claude executable" below.
agent.autoApproveDesc: Claude keeps editing the drawing without confirmation. Every edit can be undone (always on in A1)
agent.autoReadDesc: Shares the project and netlist when a conversation starts
agent.claudePathHint: Path to the claude executable used instead of auto-detection. Leave empty to return to auto-detection.
agent.knowledgeHint: Markdown file with your own standards and house rules. It is appended after the bundled standards note, so it can override them. Leave empty to use the bundled note only.
agent.knowledgeClearedLog: Settings: knowledge file cleared (bundled standards note only)
agent.pathClearedLog: Settings: claude path reset to auto-detection
agent.providerHintApi: Talks to the Anthropic Messages API directly. Needs an API key, which is stored in your OS keychain and never written to a settings file.
agent.apiKeyHint: The key is stored in your OS keychain (macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager / Secret Service). It is never written to the settings file and never shown again after saving.
agent.apiKeyEmpty: Enter an API key before saving.
agent.apiKeySavedLog: Settings: Anthropic API key saved to the OS keychain
agent.apiKeyRemovedLog: Settings: Anthropic API key removed from the OS keychain
agent.apiModelHint: Model ID used for the API route. Leave empty to return to claude-sonnet-5.
agent.testNeedsKey: Save an API key first, then test the connection.
agent.keychainError: The OS keychain could not be read, so a saved key may show as missing: {reason}
agent.providerHintCopilot: Runs the GitHub Copilot CLI on this machine and uses its own GitHub sign-in. MadakeCAD never stores a GitHub token.
agent.copilotMissingHint: Install the CLI with {command}, or set a path in "Copilot executable" below.
agent.copilotModelHint: Model used through Copilot. Leave empty (or "auto") to let Copilot choose.
agent.copilotPathHint: Path to the copilot executable used instead of auto-detection. Leave empty to return to auto-detection.
agent.copilotTestHint: The test sends one very short prompt through Copilot, which uses a small amount of your AI credits.
agent.copilotPathClearedLog: Settings: copilot path reset to auto-detection
agent.providerHintOpenAi: Talks to any OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint (OpenAI, xAI, OpenRouter, an in-house gateway, or a local Ollama). Set the URL and the model name; a key is stored in your OS keychain and is not needed for a local server.
agent.openaiUrlHint: Base URL one level above /chat/completions. Leave empty to return to https://api.openai.com/v1.
agent.openaiModelHint: Model name as the endpoint knows it. There is no default because it differs per service (for Ollama, a name from "ollama list").
agent.openaiKeyHint: The key is stored in your OS keychain, never in the settings file, and is never shown again after saving.
agent.openaiKeyLocalHint: This URL points at your own machine, so no API key is needed (Ollama does not ask for one). A key is only used if you save one.
agent.openaiTestHint: Set the URL and the model name (and a key for a remote service), then test the connection.
agent.openaiKeySavedLog: Settings: OpenAI-compatible API key saved to the OS keychain
agent.openaiKeyRemovedLog: Settings: OpenAI-compatible API key removed from the OS keychain
agent.providerHintGemini: Talks to the Google Gemini API directly. Needs a Gemini API key (from Google AI Studio), which is stored in your OS keychain and never written to a settings file.
agent.geminiModelHint: Gemini model used for the API route. Leave empty to return to gemini-2.5-flash.
agent.geminiKeyHint: The key is stored in your OS keychain, never in the settings file, and is never shown again after saving. It is sent only in the x-goog-api-key header, never in a URL.
agent.geminiKeySavedLog: Settings: Gemini API key saved to the OS keychain
agent.geminiKeyRemovedLog: Settings: Gemini API key removed from the OS keychain
agent.geminiTestHint: Save a Gemini API key first, then test the connection.

testError.openai_server: The endpoint reported a server-side error. Try again in a moment.
testError.openai_network: Could not reach the endpoint. Check the URL above, and that a local server (such as Ollama) is running.

testError.gemini_unknown: The Gemini API returned an error. Check the model name and the key above.

testError.gemini_no_model: Enter a model name first, then test the connection.

revisions.title: Edit revision table
revisions.note: ISO 7200 / JIS Z 8311: the table sits directly above the title block and stacks from old at the bottom to newest at the top.
revisions.hint: Marks advance automatically (A, B, C ...). Saving runs one command (undoable) and updates the revision table and the title block Rev.
revisions.empty: No revisions yet. Use "+ Add revision" to add the first one.
revisions.savedLog: Revision table: saved {count} row(s) (undo with Cmd+Z)
revisions.noSheetLog: Revision table: no sheet is open

wireNumbers.title: Automatic wire numbering
wireNumbers.note: IEC 62491: one number per net. It is drawn once at a representative spot on the drawing and follows through to the wire list.
wireNumbers.zoneDisabled: Zone based numbering is planned for a later phase (M4)
wireNumbers.zoneDisabledLog: Wire numbers: zone based numbering is planned for a later phase (M4)
wireNumbers.startInvalid: Enter a whole number of 1 or more.
wireNumbers.existingKeep: Keep them (number only what has none)
wireNumbers.doneSheetLog: Wire numbers: numbered {count} net(s) on "{sheet}" (undo with Cmd+Z)
wireNumbers.doneProjectLog: Wire numbers: numbered {count} net(s) across the project (undo with Cmd+Z)
wireNumbers.noSheetLog: Wire numbers: no sheet is open
wireNumbers.invalidLog: Wire numbers: the start number must be a whole number of 1 or more
wireNumbers.setLog: Wire numbers: wire number set to {number} (undo with Cmd+Z)
wireNumbers.clearedLog: Wire numbers: wire number cleared (undo with Cmd+Z)

harness.ribbonHint: Encloses a group of wires that are made and bought as one bundle; the harness name fills the harness column of the wire list. To outline an enclosure or a case, use a graphics rectangle instead - it leaves the reports alone.
harness.startLog: Harness: drag a rectangle around the wires to enclose (Esc to cancel)
harness.createdLog: Harness: created {name} enclosing {count} wire(s) (undo with Cmd+Z)
harness.kindHint: A harness boundary groups wires. An enclosure or a highlight box is drawn with a graphics rectangle, which never reaches the reports.
harness.nameHint: Harness name (W1, W2 ...). It appears in the harness column of the wire list.
harness.wireCountHint: exported in the wire list as {name}
harness.wireCountHintUnnamed: name it to have it exported in the wire list

wireLegend.ribbonHint: Places a wire part-number legend block: colour, gauge, part number and total length, derived from this sheet's wires every time it is drawn. It never reaches the netlist, the checks or the parts list.
wireLegend.startLog: Wire legend: click on the schematic sheet to place the block (Esc to cancel)
wireLegend.placedLog: Wire legend: placed the legend block (undo with Cmd+Z)

prop.title: Wire legend block
prop.hint: The legend is derived from the wires on this sheet every time it is drawn, so it never needs editing by hand.

xref.propertyHint: Sheets and zones where the same net label continues. Click an address to jump there.
xref.noneHint: no same-named net label on another sheet

ribbon.placeholder: The "{tab}" tab is planned for a later phase
ribbon.todoLog: {name}: not implemented (planned for a later phase)
ribbon.simDoneLog: SIM  DC operating point solved ({count} components)

templates.title: Start from a template
templates.undoHint: Applying is a single edit, so one Cmd+Z takes it back if it does not fit.
templates.folderOpenedLog: Templates: opened {path} (drop .json files there to see them listed)
templates.folderHintLog: Templates: drop .json files into {path} to see them listed

frameTemplates.title: Frame template
frameTemplates.noSheet: No sheet is open, so there is nothing to preview
frameTemplates.noBinds: This title block holds fixed text only
frameTemplates.info: Paper {paper} mm · Zones {zones} · Title block {titleBlock} mm · Revision table up to {revisionRows} rows
frameTemplates.scopeProjectHint: Every sheet of the open drawing switches to this frame in one edit, so Cmd+Z takes it back.
frameTemplates.scopeGlobalHint: The open drawing is left alone: new drawings will start with this frame.
frameTemplates.bindsHint: Binds are filled in while drawing. A bind nobody knows stays empty instead of breaking the sheet.
frameTemplates.zoneReadOnly: These are the divisions the frame suggests for new sheets. Each sheet keeps its own division so the zone addresses in the drawing never move.
frameTemplates.bulkHint: Switching the frame redraws the frame, the title block and the revision table of every sheet, in the canvas and in the SVG/PDF output alike.
frameTemplates.undoHint: Applying is a single edit, so one Cmd+Z takes it back.
frameTemplates.issue: Frame template could not be read: {path} ({message})
frameTemplates.openLog: Frame template: the picker is open
frameTemplates.appliedLog: Frame template: every sheet now uses "{frame}" (undo with Cmd+Z)
frameTemplates.defaultSavedLog: Frame template: new drawings will start with "{frame}"
frameTemplates.unchangedLog: Frame template: "{frame}" was already in use, nothing changed
frameTemplates.folderOpenedLog: Frame template: opened {path} (drop .json files there to see them listed)
frameTemplates.folderHintLog: Frame template: drop .json files into {path} to see them listed

symbolEditor.title: Symbol editor
symbolEditor.noPins: No connection points yet (add them with the buttons below or the pin tool)

toolName.select: Select (click to grab, drag to move, Delete to remove)
toolName.circle: Circle (drag from the centre for the radius)
toolName.arc: Arc (drag from the centre; spans 90 degrees clockwise)
toolName.text: Text (places the text from the coordinate bar)
toolName.slot: Attribute text (places the unplaced keys in order)

symbolEditor.variantsHint: Point numbers and attribute positions follow the rotation automatically (variants are not stored).

pins_grid.ok: All {count} connection points on the 2.5 mm grid
pins_grid.error: A connection point is off the grid (or there is none)

pin_numbers.error: Two connection points sit on the same position (or a number is empty)

slot_required.error: The reference designator (TAG) slot is missing

symbol.id_invalid: An ID may only use letters, digits, underscore and hyphen: {id}
symbol.id_reserved: This ID belongs to a bundled symbol (existing drawings would change): {id}
symbol.ref_prefix_empty: Enter the reference designator prefix (K, PB, ...)
symbol.no_primitives: There is no shape yet (draw a line, rectangle or circle)
symbol.pin_number_empty: A connection point has no number ({x}, {y})
symbol.pin_off_grid: Connection point {number} is off the 2.5 mm grid ({x}, {y})
symbol.pin_duplicate: Connection point {number} appears twice at the same position ({x}, {y})
symbol.pin_overlap: Connection points {other} and {number} sit on the same position ({x}, {y})
symbol.slot_missing: The reference designator slot ({key}) is required
symbol.slot_height: Attribute slot {key} has a text height of zero or less

symbolEditor.pinHint: Connection points must sit on a grid intersection
symbolEditor.noPath: Enter an ID to choose the save path
symbolEditor.openLog: Symbol editor: opened (you can start from a copy of an existing symbol)
symbolEditor.discardedLog: Symbol editor: closed and discarded the changes
symbolEditor.savedLog: Symbol editor: saved {id} to {path} (it now appears under User in Insert part)
symbolEditor.duplicatedLog: Symbol editor: started editing {id} as a copy of {source}
symbolEditor.folderOpenedLog: Symbol editor: opened {path} (drop .json files here to see them listed)
symbolEditor.folderHintLog: Symbol editor: drop .json files into {path} to see them listed

macros.basePointAuto: Bottom-left pin of the selection ({x}, {y} mm)
macros.variantAddHint: Adding variants comes in a later phase. A macro is saved as variant A for now.
macros.saveHint: Reference designators and wire numbers are stored as they are, then renumbered or cleared on insert. Saved in: {path}
macros.noSelectionLog: Macro: select the circuit to save first
macros.empty: No macros yet. Select a circuit and use Save macro.
macros.valueSetHint: A value set fills the ratings and part numbers of this macro in one go (e.g. motor rating drives the breaker rating and the wire size).
macros.valueSetNoneHint: This macro has no value set. Define placeholders and value sets when saving it.
macros.placeholderHint: Give a key name to the fields that are decided per job. Fields sharing one key are filled together by a value set.
macros.placeholderEmpty: The selection has no symbol to give a key to.
macros.valueSetNeedsKeys: Give a key to at least one field to build a value set.

macros.copiedLog: Copied {count} entities: Cmd+V to place them (reference designators are renumbered)
macros.pasteLog: PASTE  click a position (R to rotate, Esc to cancel)

blockEditor.title: Edit the pin table of {reference}
blockEditor.pinTableHint: Pin numbers are unique within the block; pins sit on a 5 mm pitch
blockEditor.previewUnavailable: The preview needs a pin table without problems

issue.emptyNo: Row {row} of the {side} has a name but no pin number
issue.sizeTooSmall: The outline is too small for these pins (at least {w}x{h} mm)

blockEditor.wiredWarning: Pins {pins} are wired: renumbering or deleting them disconnects those wires
blockEditor.placeHint: Place puts a ghost on the cursor (R rotates, Esc cancels)

blockEditor.applyHint: Applying counts as one edit, so Cmd+Z takes it back
blockEditor.editHint: Edit the pins of this block (numbers, names, order and outline)
blockEditor.droppedLog: Pins {pins} are gone: their wires are no longer connected

symbolPicker.title: Insert a part
symbolPicker.partsHint: Placing a part fills in its part number and rating (register parts with madake parts or the AI chat)
symbolPicker.placeLog: INSERT  placing symbol [{symbol}]: click a position (R to rotate, Esc to cancel)
symbolPicker.placePartLog: INSERT  placing part [{part}]: click a position (R to rotate, Esc to cancel)
symbolPicker.noSymbolLog: Part {part}: no default symbol, or the symbol is unknown (symbol_id: {symbol})

reports.title: Generate report
reports.note: Reports are derived from the drawing every time they are generated; they are never edited by hand.
reports.targetHint: The terminal chart and the connection diagram can be limited to one terminal block.
reports.formatHint: The drawing sheet is an A4 landscape page with the JIS frame and title block, split over pages as needed.
reports.diagramPdfOnly: The connection diagram is a drawing, so it comes as a PDF only.
reports.pathPlaceholder: Absolute path of the output file

pdfBook.title: Export the whole drawing set as one PDF
pdfBook.note: Page order: cover (project name, sheet list, latest revision), every schematic sheet, then the reports you pick.
pdfBook.openLog: PDF book: pick the reports to bind after the schematics

terminals.title: Terminal strip editor
terminals.noBlocks: This sheet has no terminal block yet. Place one from Insert part.
terminals.jumperHint: Select neighbouring terminals and add a saddle jumper. Every edit goes through a command, so Cmd+Z takes it back.
terminals.hint: The grid is derived from the drawing (wiring, wire numbers and wires cannot be edited here). The inside of the panel is the left connection point, the outside is the right one.
terminals.openLog: Terminal editor: editing the terminal blocks of "{sheet}"
terminals.noSheetLog: Terminal editor: no sheet is open
terminals.noBlockLog: Terminal editor: this sheet has no terminal block
terminals.jumperAddedLog: Terminal editor: jumper {jumper} added to {reference} (undo with Cmd+Z)
terminals.jumperRemovedLog: Terminal editor: jumpers on terminal(s) {terminals} of {reference} removed (undo with Cmd+Z)
terminals.chartLog: Terminal editor: wrote the chart of {reference} ({count} row(s)) to {path}
terminals.diagramLog: Terminal editor: wrote the connection diagram of {reference} ({count} page(s)) to {path}
terminals.gotoHint: Double-click a row to jump to it on the drawing
terminals.sortChangedLog: Terminal editor: {reference} sorted by {order} (undo with Cmd+Z)
terminals.gotoLog: Terminal editor: jumped to {reference} on the drawing

renumber.description: Renumbers every terminal of this block in pin order. The chart, the terminal diagram and the drawing all follow.
renumber.note: The jumper and pin-group specs are rewritten to the new numbers in the same command, so one undo puts everything back.
renumber.targetSelectedHint: Renumbering only the selected rows is planned for a later phase
renumber.issueDuplicate: The terminal numbers would repeat ({label} appears {count} times). The drawing is left unchanged.
renumber.issueEmpty: A terminal number would come out empty. The drawing is left unchanged.
renumber.issueComma: A terminal number would contain a comma ({label}), which is the separator of the stored list. The drawing is left unchanged.
renumber.issueInvalid: These numbers cannot be applied. The drawing is left unchanged.

terminals.renumberedLog: Terminal editor: renumbered {reference} from {from} to {to} (undo with Cmd+Z)

plcIo.title: PLC I/O assignment table
plcIo.note: The target and the wire number come from the drawing (read only). The signal name and the comment are owned by this table and are printed on the generated I/O sheet.
plcIo.noModules: No PLC module is placed yet. Place one from Insert part (parts library category "plc").

placement.share-if-fits: Share with the previous module when it fits
placement.share-or-split: Share and split the module when needed

plcIo.generateNote: One point becomes one rung, numbered in address order with the signal name written next to it. The page is created with a single edit, so Cmd+Z removes it again. The settings are kept for this session only.
plcIo.openLog: PLC I/O: editing the assignment table of the placed modules
plcIo.noSheetLog: PLC I/O: no sheet is open
plcIo.noModuleLog: PLC I/O: no PLC module is placed in this project
plcIo.autoNumberLog: PLC I/O: addresses of {reference} filled from {start}
plcIo.savedLog: PLC I/O: saved {count} row(s) of {reference} (undo with Cmd+Z)

plcIo.generatedLog: PLC I/O: generated the I/O sheet of {reference} (rung spacing {spacing}mm, undo with Cmd+Z)
plcIo.generateFailedLog: PLC I/O: could not generate the I/O sheet of {reference}

search.hint: Enter = next result, Shift+Enter = previous, Esc = close

devices.empty: No devices yet. Place parts with a reference designator and they show up here
devices.hint: Click a row to jump to it in the drawing. Right-click to jump or delete
devices.phase3Hint: Dragging unplaced functions onto the drawing comes in phase 3
devices.deletedLog: Devices: deleted {reference} from the drawing ({count} items — Cmd+Z undoes it)

surfer.hint: Alt-click to open. Cycle with the arrow keys and Enter, Esc closes

tidy.title: Tidy up automatically
tidy.description: Improves the drawing by repeated passes
tidy.startedLog: AGENT   Tidying up ({mode}) - one turn, undo with Cmd+Z
tidy.busyLog: AGENT   The agent is still answering; wait until the turn is done
tidy.sendFailed: AGENT   Could not send the tidy request (see the error in the chat)
tidy.variantStartedLog: AGENT   Tidying up ({mode}) as {count} variants - one conversation each, running in parallel; pick one in the comparison panel
tidy.variantNoSheetLog: AGENT   No sheet is open to make tidy variants of
tidy.variantBusyLog: AGENT   A variant comparison is in progress; adopt or discard it before starting another
tidy.variantStartFailedLog: AGENT   Could not start the tidy variants: {message}

history.head: CONVERSATIONS
history.colorDot: Edit highlight color of this conversation

parallel.runningBadgeTitle: {count} conversation(s) are answering right now. Their edits are highlighted in the drawing, one color per conversation.

dock.reloadFailedLog: AGENT   Could not reload the conversation history: {error}
dock.connectFailedLog: AGENT   Could not connect to the agent: {error}
dock.emptyConnected: Tell the agent what to do with the drawing. Edits are applied automatically and can be undone later.
dock.emptyDisconnected: No AI provider is ready. Pick one in Settings > Agent (Claude Code CLI, API key, Copilot CLI, Ollama, ...).

panel.placeholder: Ask for anything... (e.g. add a fuse to the 24 V rail)

context.head: Add context
context.attachNote: Attaching images/files is planned for phase A2
context.partsDbNote: Parts database references are planned for phase 2
context.standards: Pick a standard... (JIS C 0617 and others)
context.standardsNote: Standard references are planned for phase 2

view.wireNotesHint: Gauge, colour and cut length printed along every wire. Always exported to SVG/PDF; this toggle only hides it on screen.
view.shapesHint: Rectangles, lines, circles and polylines drawn as pure graphics. They carry no electrical meaning.

annotationText.hint: The size of the wire notes, wire numbers and net tags. It is a drawing standard, so it is set per sheet. Leave it empty for the default (2.0mm).
annotationText.range: {min}-{max}mm. On a drawing where devices sit on a 5mm pitch, about 1.4mm keeps a note off the row below.

netLabel.tagHint: Draws the net label as a directional flag, so the reader sees at a glance which way the signal goes.
netLabel.tagChangedLog: Net label {name}: tag shape set to {tag}

note.anchorHint: Which part of the text sits on the note's coordinate. Use "Right" for notes against devices on the right-hand side so their right edges line up whatever the text length.
note.colorHint: Pick the note colour from a fixed set of names. Screen and paper each get a colour that reads well there, so raw colour codes are not accepted.
note.functionHint: What this device does, printed under the symbol (the third text field after the designator and the type number).

relay.deviceBlockHint: Draws this coil as one outline with the designator, part number and a contact image (pin numbers and drawing address for every contact sharing this designator), instead of the small coil symbol and a separate contact map. The contacts stay individually placed and wired; only the coil's own drawing changes.

mate.hint: The reference designator of the mating connector (plug↔socket). Declaring it on both connectors links the pair; the wire list and from-to report carry a mate column, and a short dashed line is drawn automatically when both are on the same sheet within 50mm.

projectInfo.title: Project information
projectInfo.note: Name and number are set on the project. Company, drawing number and title are written to every sheet's title block at once.
projectInfo.name: Project name
projectInfo.hint: Saving runs one command (undoable). Only the fields you changed are written; the title block fields overwrite every sheet. The company, drawing number and title shown here are read from the sheet you are on, and saving applies them to all of them.

sheetPaper.title: Change paper — {sheet}
sheetPaper.note: Existing entities keep their coordinates; nothing is moved or deleted. Anything left outside the new paper is reported as an ERC warning instead.
sheetPaper.savedLog: Paper size: saved for "{sheet}" (undo with Cmd+Z)
sheetPaper.noSheetLog: Paper size: no sheet is open

panel.head: Unplaced parts (from the schematic)
panel.empty: Every part on the schematic is already on a panel.
panel.hint: Click a part, then click on the panel sheet to place it. It snaps onto a DIN rail; R turns it.
panel.errorHint: The list of unplaced parts could not be read: {error}

statusHint.sized: The outline comes from the parts database.
statusHint.default: The part number has no outline in the parts database, so the default rectangle is used.
statusHint.unregistered: This part has no part number yet, so the default rectangle is used.

panel.placeLog: Panel: placing {reference} — click on the panel (R turns it, Esc cancels)
panel.schematicToolLog: The schematic tools (wiring, part insertion …) cannot be used on a panel layout sheet.
panel.panelToolLog: The panel tools (enclosure, DIN rail, duct) can only be used on a panel layout sheet.

toolLog.panel_outline: Enclosure: drag a rectangle for the panel (Esc to cancel)
toolLog.din_rail: DIN rail: drag horizontally at the mounting line (Esc to cancel)
toolLog.duct: Duct: drag a rectangle for the wiring duct (Esc to cancel)
toolLog.panel_legend: Legend table: click on the panel sheet to place the table (Esc to cancel)

added.panel_outline: Panel: added an enclosure (undo with Cmd+Z)
added.din_rail: Panel: added a DIN rail (undo with Cmd+Z)
added.duct: Panel: added a wiring duct (undo with Cmd+Z)

prop.referenceHint: The reference designator links the footprint to the schematic part. Change it on the schematic symbol.
prop.name: Name
prop.legendHint: The legend is derived from the parts on this sheet every time it is drawn, so it never needs editing by hand.

panel.todoPhase: Planned for a later phase of the panel layout work
panel.legendPlacedLog: Panel: placed the legend table (undo with Cmd+Z)
panel.balloonDoneLog: Panel: numbered {count} part(s) in reading order (undo with Cmd+Z)
panel.balloonEmptyLog: Panel: there is no part on this sheet to number yet.
panel.clearanceDoneLog: Panel checks done: {error} error(s) / {warning} warning(s) / {info} note(s) — see the verification panel

sheets.addHint: Pick what the new sheet is for.

wireParts.autoHint: The part number looked up from the wire-part table by colour and gauge. A wire with an empty part number is listed with this one.
wireParts.manualHint: A part number written here wins over the wire-part table. Leave it empty to take the number from the table.

shapes.ribbonHint: Draw an enclosure, a highlight box or a note frame. Graphics carry no electrical meaning, so they never reach the netlist, the checks or any report.

startLog.rect: Rectangle: drag to draw (Esc to cancel)
startLog.line: Line: drag from one end to the other (Esc to cancel)
startLog.circle: Circle: drag from the centre outwards (Esc to cancel)
startLog.polyline: Polyline: click each corner, double-click or Enter to finish (Esc to cancel)

added.rect: Graphics: added a rectangle (undo with Cmd+Z)
added.line: Graphics: added a line (undo with Cmd+Z)
added.circle: Graphics: added a circle (undo with Cmd+Z)
added.polyline: Graphics: added a polyline (undo with Cmd+Z)

shapes.polylineHint: Click each corner in turn, then double-click or press Enter to finish.
shapes.strokeHint: Pick the colour from a fixed set of names, the same ones the notes use. Screen and paper each get a colour that reads well there, so raw colour codes are not accepted.
shapes.fillHint: Shades the inside of the shape. The fill is kept light so the wires and symbols underneath stay readable.

prop.hint: A shape is drawing only: it never appears in the netlist, the checks, the parts list or the wire list. Draw enclosures with a shape and keep harness boundaries for grouping wires.
